title: Deluge
descript: Deluge is a BitTorrent client. Its daemon runs in the container and is driven from the Deluge Web UI on port 8020. Sign in with the default password deluge, then change it. The Web UI adds torrent files, magnet links and URLs, shows download and seeding progress and sets speed limits. Settings and resume data stay in DockerAppData/delugedocker/config, the payload in downloads. Only the Web UI port is published, so incoming peers need a forwarded port on the router. No telemetry is sent to the developer.
important: Default Web UI password is deluge, change it on first login. Only port 8020 (Web UI) is published. Incoming peer connections need a listen port forwarded on the router, outgoing connections work without it. Your public IP is sent to the trackers, DHT nodes and peers of every torrent you add and no VPN is included. Data lives in DockerAppData/delugedocker. The page is plain HTTP on the LAN, so use a TLS reverse proxy before exposing it to the internet.
release_note: 2.2.0-4: rectified per review comments. F2 fixed: /run is pre-mounted as a tmpfs owned by uid 1000, so s6-overlay no longer aborts with exit code 100 before Deluge starts. C9 fixed: app.lang no longer uses ASCII semicolons, which the store parser treated as a comment and cut the description, and the text describes only delivered features. P2 fixed: help points to a rendered help page. S11 fixed: umask 027 and owner-only /config. T1 fixed: image bumped to ls388.

data_notes: `config` holds the daemon and web settings (auth, core.conf, torrents.state, plugins); `downloads` holds the torrent payload and is the default save path. Copying `config` keeps the client configuration; `downloads` is your own data.
design_notes: **Runs as a non-root container.** uid/gid 1000, `cap_drop: [ALL]` and `no-new-privileges`; `CapEff=0000000000000000` measured inside the running container. The entrypoint wrapper sets `umask 027`, keeps `/config` owner-only (0700 dirs, 0600 files, the credential hash is 0600) and `/downloads` group-readable (0750) so nothing is world writable.
**Two volumes.** `/config` keeps the daemon/web settings; `/downloads` receives the torrent data.
**Health check** probes the web UI on container port 8112 (curl ships with the image).
**Fixed image tag pinned by digest**, Docker Hub only (ls388, build date 2026-11-24), no `privileged`, no `network_mode: host`, no Docker socket, no `cap_add`.
**No telemetry to the developer.** The only traffic is the BitTorrent traffic your own torrents generate, plus the daemon's optional release check (settings -> Other).

**`/run` is a tmpfs owned by uid 1000** so s6-overlay starts even when the install-time `/run` has another owner. Without it the image's preinit aborts with exit code 100 and the container restarts in a loop (the start-up failure seen on 2.2.0-3).
limitations: Only the web UI port (8020) is published. The container uses bridge networking, so the daemon's UPnP/NAT-PMP request cannot open a port on your router. Incoming peer connections therefore need a listen port forwarded manually on the router. Outgoing connections, trackers and DHT still work without it.

Adding a torrent announces it to that torrent's trackers and to the DHT, so your public IP, client port and up/download counters become visible to those third parties. LSD (local peer discovery) also broadcasts on the LAN. There is no anonymity layer of any kind.
No VPN is included. Pair it with a VPN tunnel or a trusted network if your torrent traffic must not be attributable to your line.
The page is plain HTTP on the LAN and ships with the upstream default password `deluge`; change it on first login and use a TLS reverse proxy before exposing the UI to the internet.
Optional outbound checks can be switched off: settings -> Other -> 'Check for new releases' (on by default, every 3 days) and 'Send anonymous stats' (off by default).
`/downloads` belongs to this app only and is not shared with other download/media packages; add the same path to them if you want a shared library.
Docker applications cannot be upgraded in place in the App Center: updating means uninstalling and reinstalling, which keeps the data folders.

runtime_files.purpose: web UI and daemon credentials (salted hash, never the plain password)
runtime_files.lifecycle: written when the password changes; back it up

runtime_files.purpose: daemon preferences: listen ports, bandwidth limits, DHT/UPnP/encryption switches, proxy
torrent list, labels/queue order and resume data for the torrents you add
runtime_files.created: when the first torrent is added
runtime_files.growth: grows with the number of torrents
runtime_files.lifecycle: rewritten periodically; deleting it loses queue/resume state, not the payload

runtime_files.purpose: web UI allow-list and local daemon entry (host id, 127.0.0.1:58846)
configuration and state of the plugins you enable
the torrent payload and the default save path
runtime_files.lifecycle: yours; kept on uninstall unless you ask to delete data
